$schema_note: Parity task suite. Each task is a deterministic script of MCP tool calls against a disposable fixture plus an oracle check defined BEFORE execution. Step forms: {call, args, [expect_error]} | {expect:{path, equals|gte|contains|not_equals}} | {sleep} | {key} (shorthand for call key). Coordinate sugar: target {client:[x,y]} = fixture client-relative point converted to a coordinate target in the latest full-screen raster; {client_zoom:[x,y]} = point inside the latest zoom raster; region {client:[x,y,w,h]} for zoom. {window:'second'} on a client target aims at the fixture's second window instead of the main one. target {window_title:'<title>', at:[x,y]} = a point inside a non-fixture window (native dialogs/choosers) found by title on the work display; negative at[] components measure back from the far edge. Every task is repeated `repeats` times from a fresh fixture. Steps that need accessibility are marked optional_a11y and count as 'untested' (not failed) when get_app_state cannot see the app.

tasks.goal: Fill name, tick checkbox, choose select value by keyboard, submit; verify submitted payload.
Switch tabs B then C then A; panel state follows.
Click Load; a premature click during loading must not confirm; after ready, Confirm succeeds.

known_limitations.linux-xvfb: reps right after a fixture relaunch raced the oracle: the window mapped before Chromium published the CU-FIXTURE title state, so the first expect sampled nulls (observed 2026-09-16 as 1/5 then 2/5 fails across two runs). The X11 driver now waits for a readable oracle state before launchFixture returns; kept as a note on what the wait is for.
known_limitations.win32-desktop: no equivalent race: the win32 driver gates fixture readiness on the page's own beacon, so the oracle is live before the first step.

tasks.goal: Scroll the list to the bottom and click the Reveal button that only exists on the last row.
Click a button inside a same-document iframe; parent receives the message.
Drag the chip onto the drop zone.
tasks.skip: held-input gestures require a persistent input owner — the desktop helper or the agent --serve route; the direct in-process MCP surface refuses them (input_owner_required) by design so a disconnected client cannot leave buttons held

known_limitations.linux-xvfb: no Linux desktop helper exists; the local route has no input owner and left_click_drag is refused input_owner_required. The 2026-09-07 receipt predates the input-owner guard — its 5/5 for this row is stale.
known_limitations.linux-x11: no Linux desktop helper exists; the local route refuses left_click_drag (input_owner_required). Held input is possible through the ssh agent --serve route, which is a separate surface this suite does not run.
known_limitations.win32-desktop: no Windows desktop helper exists; the local route has no input owner and held-input gestures are refused input_owner_required, by the same design as the Linux direct route.

tasks.goal: Open the native file chooser from <input type=file>, type the fixture upload path, confirm; page reads the file contents.

known_limitations.linux-xvfb: Chromium's GTK file chooser commits a typed location-entry path only via the Open button — Return in the entry closes the dialog with no selection (a stock GTK3 FileChooserDialog commits the same path on Return, so this is Chromium's wrapper). The dialog also carries no AT-SPI elements, so only a window-relative pointer click reaches it.
known_limitations.linux-x11: same Chromium chooser behavior: type the path, then click Open; Return in the location entry discards it. On desktops where xdg-desktop-portal supplies the chooser instead, the dialog is a different application entirely and this window_title target will not resolve — record that honestly if it shows.
known_limitations.win32-desktop: Windows common file dialog: the File name field owns focus when it opens, so a typed absolute path + Return commits. No location-bar gesture is needed.

tasks.goal: Click the download link; a file with the expected contents lands in the run's download dir.
Type accented text, CJK and an emoji into an input; value round-trips exactly.

known_limitations.linux-xvfb: non-ASCII chars go through per-char `key U<hex>` (deterministic case fix), but under heavy host load XTEST can still drop a remapped char — observed 2026-09-16 as a single missing é/日 in ~1/5 reps. A delivery-layer flake on a loaded container, not a mapping defect; a starved Xvfb run is exactly where it shows.

tasks.goal: Send a ctrl+shift chord and a plain key; the page sees exactly those chords.
Zoom into the tab strip and click Tab C using coordinates in the ZOOM raster; verifies child-raster coordinate transform live.
A coordinate outside the zoom raster is refused before any input is sent.

known_limitations.win32-desktop: SendInput clamps out-of-range absolute coordinates rather than erroring at the OS level; this row verifies the backend refuses before dispatch, not that Windows refuses.

tasks.goal: Observe the page through accessibility, click 'Tab B' by element target, verify via oracle.
After the observed element disappears (Load replaces it), acting on the old element target fails element_stale instead of clicking something else.
Type into the entry and press Apply; label shows the applied text.
Open the File menu with the pointer and pick 'Mark file' by pointer click (Tk posted menus do not receive synthetic keys in this environment).
Wheel-scroll the listbox down then click a visible row; a row beyond the first page is selected.
Drag the square into the zone.

tasks.goal: Open a modal dialog; while it is open, clicking Apply must NOT apply; answer the dialog with the keyboard.

known_limitations.linux-x11: KWin does not give the transient Tk dialog X input focus, so typed text does not reach it; passes on the isolated Xvfb route
known_limitations.linux-xvfb: Tk's simpledialog is toolkit-modal only: it sets WM_TRANSIENT_FOR + grab_set but no _NET_WM_STATE_MODAL, so a stacking WM lets the parent Apply click take X input focus (verified under openbox and metacity). The grab still blocks the click (applied stays empty) but the typed answer then goes to the parent and the dialog stays open. Passes where the WM keeps focus on the transient.
known_limitations.win32-desktop: Tk maps grab_set to a real OS-level capture on Windows, so the parent click should not steal focus the way X11 stacking WMs allow; if it fails anyway that is a Tk/Windows behavior worth recording, not an engine defect.

tasks.goal: Open a second window and click a button inside it, targeting by that window's own origin.
Type accented text and an emoji into a Tk entry and apply it.

known_limitations.linux-xvfb: per-char `key U<hex>` + `shift+` for cased capitals fixes the level-0 lowercase remap (Ü→ü). Residual: under heavy host load XTEST can still drop a remapped char — an X11 delivery characteristic, not a mapping defect.

tasks.goal: Triple-click selects the whole entry text.
A ctrl chord reaches the entry with the modifier state intact.
With no display session the probe reports an actionable failure and screenshot fails closed (no silent success).
tasks.skip: there is no display-session env to blank on Windows; the refusal this task exercises (no session -> actionable DISPLAY error) has no win32 equivalent. The honest Windows analogue is a missing PowerShell/UIA capability, which cannot be induced per-task.

known_limitations.win32-desktop: skipped: no display-session concept to deny; UIA + SendInput need no per-session grant on the interactive desktop.

tasks.goal: A cancelled in-flight request gets no response, the next request is served, and no action is replayed.
After stop_computer_control, pointer actions are refused and the fixture sees no click.
Restart the server mid-task: old state_ids and rasters are rejected on the new session (no stale replay), a fresh screenshot works.
